account: ARMMAN tested a scheduler that selected mothers for live calls within its mMitra health-information program in India. The seven-week study began on 26 April 2021 and included 23,003 women. Participants received regular recorded messages, with two groups also receiving staff calls allocated either by the model or in rotation. Model-selected calls reduced cumulative engagement drops by 32.0% compared with messaging alone (p = .044) and by 28.3% compared with rotation-based calls (p = .098). The outcome counted weekly listening and did not measure clinical health. The developers report that the system, under the name SAHELI, ran in deployment from April 2022 and benefited more than 350,000 mothers. The project lasted until the summer of 2025. Later studies examined revised models and health behaviors in other cohorts.

ai_role.statement: The model selected participants for limited staff calls. The trial compared that policy with rotation-based calls and regular messaging alone. The developers and ARMMAN jointly conducted the study.
